role.altitude: The specialist stops gathering and formatting job and pay data by hand. They own the job architecture, the four-factor evaluation scheme and the evidence behind every pay difference that the pay transparency law will ask for. They decide grades, sign off figures and agree criteria with the works council. Pipelines and drafting loops do the collecting, joining and first drafts.
reach: people-analyst: run the nightly AFAS extract that feeds the job and pay data mart, and learn the data model
hrbp: use job family maps and band guidance when advising managers on roles and moves
recruiter: show the pay band in Recruitee before negotiation and drop the salary-history question
ld: run pay and benefits courses in Studytube and track who has completed them
payroll: check CAO step and scale data in AFAS against the job grade register
skills_to_grow: Four-factor job evaluation (skills, responsibilities, effort, working conditions) under EU 2023/970
Reading and checking SQL or Power BI models built on the AFAS extract
Writing prompts and acceptance checks for bounded drafting loops
Works council consultation on grading systems (WOR 27(1)(c)) and AI Act Art. 26 duties
Pay gap analysis and explaining gaps by job category
role.ambitious_version: By the first report over 2027 pay (due 7 June 2028), Noordhaven has one governed job register. It links every AFAS job code to a current description, a four-factor grade with reasons and a band, and covers agency workers too. The specialist can explain any gap of 5% or more in each category before the six-month deadline, and answers employee pay requests well within two months.

tasks.short: Research what jobs require, how jobs relate to each other, and sector trends affecting Noordhaven's roles.

steps.what: Collect job codes, headcount, grades and existing descriptions per function
Interview managers and watch warehouse and transport work on site
Scan sector trends: CAO regrading, salary surveys, AI and job change

loop.input: Saved CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer bulletins, survey reports and pension fund notices
loop.output: Short dated summary per source with quotes and links
loop.check: Each claim must carry a quote and a source link; the specialist spot-checks
loop.stop: One pass per source; if no quote is found, mark it 'not found' instead of guessing
loop.why_not_simpler: Sources are free-text PDFs and web pages with no fixed structure

steps.what: Map job families, levels and reporting lines in a sheet
Write findings memo with proposed job changes

loop.input: Job family map, trend notes, interview notes
loop.output: Draft memo in the HR template
loop.check: Specialist reads it; every figure is pulled from the map, not written by the model
loop.stop: One draft plus one revision; after that the specialist edits by hand
loop.why_not_simpler: The memo is prose that has to tie together free-text notes

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the governed data platform reads AFAS job schemes and the SharePoint description library into a job register, and a small CRUD app on top holds job families and levels. A bounded model loop summarises saved CAO and survey documents with quotes and drafts the memo, while the specialist does the interviews and decides.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job data was split between AFAS fields and Word files on SharePoint with no shared key, and sector news only came as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a small register and an extract cheap to build, and models can now summarise CAO bulletins with quotes. AFAS Profit 8 has fields for job schemes and categories [S2].
tasks.still_hard: Working out what a reach-truck driver or planner really does still takes site visits across shifts. The sector regrading under the CAO has no outcome yet, so trends can be read in more than one way.
tasks.human_edge: Watching the work and earning managers' trust in interviews, and judging whether a role has really changed or just drifted.

ambition.what: A job-change check every quarter for the 30 largest job codes instead of ad hoc reviews every few years, regrading only when core duties have materially changed

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends this time on site and with managers rather than in spreadsheets. They gain the right to flag a job for re-evaluation from register evidence.

reach.learn: How job codes, cost centres and CAO scales link in the AFAS data model
Using the job family map to place new or changed roles

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency
61% of employers are rewriting job descriptions for AI and 49% say salary structures lag
Do not regrade if core accountabilities have not materially changed
CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are regrading the sector's jobs, with no outcome yet

assumptions: The AFAS job codes are fairly complete and up to date
The existing job descriptions are on SharePoint as Word or PDF files
unknowns: How many distinct job codes Noordhaven has across the three sites
Whether the warehouse CAO has its own job grading system
Whether there is already a governed data platform, or only the Power BI extract
research_questions: How many AFAS job codes have no matching description, or one more than three years old?
Do the trend summaries hold up when the specialist checks ten of them against the sources?
Does the works council see a job register as part of the grading system that needs its consent?

tasks.short: Decide which job analysis tools are needed and build questionnaires, interview guides and description templates.

steps.what: Find jobs with missing or outdated descriptions and evaluations
Draft four-factor questionnaire, interview guide and description template

loop.input: The four factors (skills, responsibilities, effort, working conditions), the CAO job system and the current templates
loop.output: Draft questions and template sections, each tagged with a factor
loop.check: Every factor has questions; a checklist rejects salary-history and protected-trait questions; the specialist edits
loop.stop: Two revisions at most; then manual editing
loop.why_not_simpler: The questions need plain Dutch wording for each job group, which a fixed template cannot give

steps.what: Test with managers and discuss criteria with the works council
Build the questionnaire as a form and collect answers
Revise instruments and publish the final versions

tasks.design: A Power BI page on the AFAS extract and SharePoint metadata shows which jobs lack a current description or four-factor evaluation. A bounded model loop drafts questionnaires and templates tagged by factor, and Microsoft Forms collects the answers into a SharePoint list. The specialist and the works council settle the criteria.
tasks.previous_blocker: There was no legal push for a structured four-factor scheme, and writing tailored instruments for each job group took too long to repeat.
tasks.enabler_now: The pay transparency bill sets the four factors and works council consent [S1]. Models can draft factor-tagged questions quickly, and a UK pilot graded descriptions per factor with over 70% accuracy against experts [S8].
tasks.still_hard: Getting the works council to agree on criteria and grouping, and keeping CAO-graded jobs inside the CAO system while sector regrading is still going on.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to measure and why, and building agreement with the works council and managers on fair criteria.

ambition.what: A standard four-factor job analysis kit that HRBPs can use themselves for new or changed roles

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time writing forms and more time designing the evaluation scheme. They get the right to propose the scheme to the works council.

reach.task: Run job analysis interviews for new roles
Lead the works council consent process
reach.learn: Which criteria the scheme uses and why

evidence.claim: Job evaluation on four factors; the works council consents to the system, criteria and grouping
ChatGPT scoring of job descriptions per HERA factor exceeded 70% accuracy against experts
A pay or grading system needs works council consent unless a CAO settles it
A salary-history question is not allowed

assumptions: Microsoft Forms is licensed in the M365 tenant
The specialist owns the job analysis method
unknowns: Which jobs the CAOs grade and which are outside the CAO
Whether the works council wants an external expert to review the scheme
Whether an existing method such as ORBA or Hay is used today
research_questions: Does the works council accept model-drafted instruments if the criteria are agreed first?
Do managers fill in the four-factor form for warehouse roles completely and the same way?
How far do model-drafted factor scores fall from the specialist's own grades on 20 Noordhaven jobs?

tasks.short: Analyse pay, job and sector data and supply figures to management, sector bodies and government.

steps.what: Pull salary, FTE, grade and gender data from AFAS and agencies
Clean, join and calculate gaps, costs and distributions
Interpret results and explain gaps and outliers
Answer data requests from management, CBS, sector fund and auditors

loop.input: Data request email and the approved figures from the data mart
loop.output: Draft reply or brief with tables filled by code
loop.check: Numbers come only from the query; the model writes only text around them; the specialist approves before sending
loop.stop: One draft; if the request needs data not in the mart, flag it to the specialist
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests arrive as free-text emails asking for different cuts

tasks.design: Replace the Excel workbooks that join AFAS payroll and agency pay files with a scheduled Python/SQL job on the governed data platform. It builds a pay data mart and Power BI pages for gap per category, CAO costing and headcount. A bounded loop drafts replies to data requests around query-filled tables, and the specialist explains gaps and approves anything that leaves the company.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency pay data came as separate files from three portals, and there was no legal need for gap figures by job category, so manual Excel pulls were good enough.
tasks.enabler_now: The pay transparency law requires yearly gap reports that include agency workers, with agencies supplying their pay data [S1]. AI coding makes the extract and joins cheap to build and test.
tasks.still_hard: Getting clean, timely pay data from three agencies, and explaining gaps fairly when job categories are still being redrawn. The data is confidential and some of it is special-category under the GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a gap is explained by legitimate factors, and telling the HR Director and works council an uncomfortable finding.

ambition.what: A monthly unexplained-gap check per job category instead of a once-a-year look, so gaps are fixed before the six-month joint evaluation trigger

tasks.altitude: The specialist moves from building workbooks to explaining and fixing pay differences. They gain the right to propose corrections in the yearly pay round.

reach.task: Own the pay data mart and Power BI model
reach.learn: Gap methods by job category as the law defines them

reach.task: Cost CAO increases in the budget
reach.learn: Reusing the same CAO cost model

evidence.claim: Yearly gap report, first over 2027 pay by 7 June 2028; agency workers count and agencies supply pay data
An unexplained gap of 5% or more after six months triggers a joint evaluation; fines up to EUR 11,000
Pay gap figures can be deterministic software on AFAS data

assumptions: The Power BI AFAS extract can be extended with payroll components
unknowns: In what format and how often the three agencies can deliver pay data
Who can see individual pay data in the data platform
Which external bodies send regular data requests
research_questions: Can all three agencies deliver pay per worker per job in a usable file each month?
Do the mart's figures match AFAS payroll totals to the euro for one month close?
How large is the unexplained gap per category today on 2026 data?

tasks.short: Plan, build and run training on pay policy, CAO scales, benefits and pay transparency for managers and HR.

steps.what: Identify audiences and what they need to know
Draft slides, e-learning and quick-reference sheets

loop.input: SharePoint policies, CAO articles and the training plan
loop.output: Slide outline, quiz questions and a one-page guide in Dutch
loop.check: Every rule cites a policy or CAO article; the specialist checks figures and legal points
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning policy text into plain teaching material is a writing task

steps.what: Load course into Studytube, enrol audiences, track completion
Run live sessions per site, fitted around shifts

tasks.design: A bounded model loop turns SharePoint pay policies, CAO articles and the pay transparency rules into draft slides, quizzes and one-page guides, with a citation for each rule. Studytube is set up to enrol managers, recruiters and HRBPs automatically from AFAS and to report completions. The specialist runs the live sessions at the three sites.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material was rebuilt by hand each year, and there was little need to train managers on pay rules outside the yearly pay round.
tasks.enabler_now: New duties need trained managers and recruiters: band before negotiation, no salary-history question, and pay requests answered within two months [S1]. Models draft teaching material from policy text quickly.
tasks.still_hard: Reaching shift managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, and keeping the material right while the law's start date and the CAO regrading are still open.
tasks.human_edge: Answering managers' real cases in the room and changing how they talk about pay with their teams.

ambition.what: Short pay transparency training for every shift lead and recruiter, including the rule that offers start from the band

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time making slides and more time with managers in sessions. Nothing changes in decision rights.

reach.task: Set up compliance courses in Studytube
reach.learn: Pay transparency duties managers must meet
Sharing the band before negotiation and the ban on salary-history questions

evidence.claim: Band before negotiation, no salary-history question, pay requests answered in two months
Models can draft training materials from policy documents
A benefits chatbot must say it is AI

assumptions: Studytube can enrol people by AFAS function or role group
unknowns: How many people manage staff or make offers
Whether the start date of the pay transparency law will be known in time to plan training
Whether training time for shift leads is counted as working time under the CAO
research_questions: After training, do Recruitee offers show the band and leave out salary-history questions?
Does drafting with the loop cut preparation time by at least half on one course?
What share of shift leads complete the Studytube module within a month?
